## panopt
PANopt coordination daemon: shared todos and notes across agents.
Each connection is scoped to one project by the ?ws=<project path> query parameter on the server URL.
- Registry: call identify (name, optional status) on startup so others can see you; whoami returns your own entry; agent_list returns every agent on the project (each entry's key_source is `declared` for stable `?agent=<id>` ids or `session` for the rotating MCP session id - only session entries idle-prune). Connecting already registers you. agent_leave removes your registry entry and releases your locks; the idle sweep handles agents that just disappear.
- Locks: lock_acquire (name, optional note) takes a named advisory lock and is non-blocking; lock_release frees it; lock_status lists every held lock. Locks are advisory - agents cooperate, the daemon does not enforce.
- Todos: todo_create (returns an id), todo_list (summaries), todo_get (one todo in full), todo_update (edit any field), todo_complete, todo_delete, todo_add_blocker / todo_remove_blocker / todo_set_blockers, todo_comment_add / todo_comment_update / todo_comment_delete, todo_tags_list (project tag vocabulary, union with notes), and todo_lock / todo_unlock (advisory `todo:<id>` lock, surfaced as locked_by on todo_get). Each todo also projects to .panopt/todos/<id>.md.
- Notes: note_create (returns an id), note_list, note_get (one note in full), note_append (add to body), note_read (body only), note_update (replace title, body, and/or tags), note_delete, note_tags_list (project tag vocabulary, same union as todo_tags_list). Each note also projects to .panopt/note/<id>.md.
- Agent tools (config layer): agent_tool_create (returns an id), agent_tool_list, agent_tool_get, agent_tool_update, agent_tool_delete. Durable per-project agent configurations the cockpit can spawn from. Projected to .panopt/agent_tools.md.
- Processes (instance layer): process_create (kind agent/command/terminal, optional agent_tool_id, returns an id), process_list, process_get, process_update, process_delete. Per-p… [truncated]

- verify-all: Run the full check + clippy sweep across the workspace AND the WASM plugin (panopt-zellij). Use after non-trivial edits, before declaring work done, or when asked to verify the repo builds cleanly. Captures the dual-target dance (workspace builds for host, panopt-zellij builds only for wasm32-wasip1) so you don't have to remember the right manifest-path/target each time.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

file.content:
daemon:
    cargo run -p panoptd -- --port 7600

# Tail the daemon log file written by `panopt up`.
logs:
    tail -F ~/.local/share/panopt/panoptd.log

# If a daemon is already running on port 7600, `panopt up` connects to it
# rather than restarting it - use `just stop && just up` to force a fresh
# debug daemon, or `just restart-daemon` to swap the daemon out without
# touching the cockpit.
#
# Launch the cockpit in the current project (debug binaries). Build the
# workspace AND the release wasm plugin first so `panoptd` and the sidebar
# plugin both reflect the latest sources; without these, `cargo run -p
# panopt` would happily re-spawn yesterday's `panoptd` from `target/debug/`
# and Zellij would load yesterday's plugin from
# `crates/panopt-zellij/target/wasm32-wasip1/release/panopt-zellij.wasm`
# (the path `panopt up` auto-detects in `default_plugin_wasm`).
up: plugin-release
    cargo build --workspace
    cargo run -p panopt -- up

# Stop the running panoptd (SIGTERM x2 to clear the clients-connected gate).
stop:
    -pkill -TERM -x panoptd
    @sleep 1
    -pkill -TERM -x panoptd

# Nuke EVERYTHING and start over: kill every panopt-* Zellij session (which
# tears down the loaded wasm plugin and every `_viewer` / `_agent` /
# `_process-run` subprocess), kill the daemon, rebuild workspace + release
# wasm, then `panopt up`. Use when a code change spans the daemon, the
# binaries, and/or the plugin and you want the running cockpit to actually
# reflect HEAD. Must be run from a plain shell (not inside Zellij).
refresh:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    if [ -n "${ZELLIJ:-}" ]; then
        echo "run \`just refresh\` from a plain shell, not inside Zellij" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    # `grep` exits 1 when no panopt-* sessions match - that's a clean slate,
    # not an error. Wrap so `set -o pipefail` doesn't abort the recipe when
    # there's nothing to kill (e.g. a follow-up refresh after a crash).
    zellij list-sessions -sn 2>/dev/null | { grep '^panopt-' || true; } | while read -r s; do
        zellij kill-session "$s" 2>/dev/null || true
        zellij delete-session "$s" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
    pkill -TERM -x panoptd 2>/dev/null || true
    sleep 1
    pkill -TERM -x panoptd 2>/dev/null || true
    just up

# Rebuild panoptd, stop the running daemon, and re-launch it detached. The
# cockpit's MCP clients reconnect on the next call, so this is the
# ergonomic path while a cockpit is open: edit handler code, `just
# restart-daemon`, the next autosave hits the new binary.
restart-daemon:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo build -p panoptd
    pkill -TERM -x panoptd 2>/dev/null || true
    sleep 1
    pkill -TERM -x panoptd 2>/dev/null || true
    sleep 1
    mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share/panopt"
    setsid -f target/debug/panoptd --port 7600 \
        < /dev/null \
        >> "$HOME/.local/share/panopt/panoptd.log" 2>&1
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
        if ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -q '127.0.0.1:7600'; then
            echo "panoptd restarted on 127.0.0.1:7600"
            exit 0
        fi
        sleep 0.1
    done
    echo "panoptd did not start listening within 5s; see ~/.local/share/panopt/panoptd.log" >&2
    exit 1

# Open the panopt sqlite database in the sqlite3 shell.
db:
    sqlite3 ~/.local/share/panopt/panopt.db

# Clean both target dirs.
clean:
    cargo clean
    cargo clean --manifest-path crates/panopt-zellij/Cargo.toml

# run a 'connected' agent externally (outside of panopt). this is for connecting a dev-time agent to the built system.
# Uses `panopt agent-config` so the launched session gets a stable agent id,
# a friendly display name, and the bearer token the daemon requires.
devagent name='greg-main':
    claude --mcp-config "$(cargo run -q -p panopt -- agent-config --id {{name}} --name {{name}})"

devagent_old:
    claude --mcp-config "$(cargo run -q -p panopt -- agent-config)"

374	    pub kind: String,

377	    /// Lifecycle status (`starting`/`running`/`stopped`/...), or `None` for a

384	    pub tool_type: Option<String>,

396	    pub agent_id: Option<String>,

401	    /// #190); the config-centric pane binds to a representative one (the first).
402	    /// `None` for command/terminal rows and any instance with no backing config.
403	    pub agent_tool_id: Option<u64>,
404	    /// The "sitting idle for N" age (`idle:<age>` segment, bug #163), present
405	    /// only while the agent is in the `idle` state - the daemon computes it as
406	    /// `now - state_since` and projects the formatted age. The Agents pane
407	    /// appends it to the row's status so a parked agent shows how long it has

411	}

413	/// A parsed `.panopt/agent_tools.md` line: one durable agent config (the
414	/// config layer of the two-layer model). The Agents pane is config-centric -
415	/// each config *is* an agent - so this is the row it renders, joined to a
416	/// representative live [`ProcessRow`] by `id == agent_tool_id` (the daemon is a
417	/// 1:N factory, todo #190; surfacing every instance is a follow-up).
418	/// Line format (see `render_agent_tools_md`): `- #<id> <label> [<flag>]<cmd>`.
419	pub struct ConfigRow {
420	    pub id: u64,
421	    pub label: String,
422	    /// Whether the config is offered for spawning (`[enabled]` vs `[disabled]`).
423	    pub enabled: bool,
424	}

426	/// Parse one `.panopt/agent_tools.md` config line into a [`ConfigRow`], or
427	/// `None` for the header / `_(no agent tools)_` placeholder / any malformed
428	/// line. The label runs up to the ` [<flag>]` segment; a trailing command (when
429	/// the config carries one) is ignored - the pane shows the agent, not its argv.
430	pub fn parse_config_line(line: &str) -> Option<ConfigRow> {
431	    let rest = line.trim().strip_prefix("- #")?;
432	    let space = rest.find(' ')?;
433	    let id: u64 = rest[..space].parse().ok()?;
434	    let after = &rest[space + 1..];
435	    let bracket = after.find(" [")?;
436	    let label = after[..bracket].trim().to_string();
437	    let flag_rest = &after[bracket + 2..];
438	    let close = flag_rest.find(']')?;
439	    let enabled = &flag_rest[..close] == "enabled";
440	    Some(ConfigRow { id, label, enabled })
441	}

content.text:
Root cause is now well-supported. Compare the two swap sites:
- **Normal content swap** (`main.rs:2527`): `replace_pane_with_existing_pane(slot, pane, …)` — anchored on the **designated slot** (the single shared content position).
- **Disposal swap** (`main.rs:2236`): `replace_pane_with_existing_pane(target, viewer, …)` — anchored on the **agent's own independent tile**, and it surfaces `first_suppressed_viewer()` — *any* suppressed viewer, possibly one semantically owned by the slot/swap model.

So disposal moves an arbitrary suppressed viewer into the disposed agent's tile position and desyncs the plugin's `slot_pane`/suppressed bookkeeping from Zellij's actual tiling → the jumble. Let me record this as the step-8 finding on #208:

input.body:
STEP 8 ✗ FAIL (pane suppression, #207) — BUG FOUND. Repro: fresh cockpit (refreshed @12:27, plugin wasm rebuilt), spawn_agent(name=verify-suppress) → instance #232 / ephemeral config 231, pane materialized titled "Agent #232 - verify-suppress". Then process_stop(#232)+process_delete(#232) over MCP. Daemon side correct: config 231 reaped (#205), sidebar row gone. BUT the pane did NOT cleanly suppress — operator reports the pane vanished AND the cockpit layout became "a jumble" (panes reshuffled / corrupted). The #207 contract is suppress-not-close with the user able to resurface; instead the layout broke.

ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (main.rs suppress_pane, added in 9935faa):
- Agent/command/terminal panes are INDEPENDENT panes (per the crate-level doc: "agents, commands, and terminals are each their own pane"), not the single shared swap-in-place content viewer. suppress_pane treats the disposed agent tile like the content slot: replace_pane_with_existing_pane(target=agent_tile, viewer=first_suppressed_viewer(), true) surfaces an ARBITRARY suppressed viewer into the agent's tiled position. That viewer may be one owned by the slot/swap-in-place model, so the plugin's slot_pane/suppressed bookkeeping desyncs from Zellij's actual tiling → reshuffle.
- Contrast: the normal content swap (main.rs:2527) anchors on the designated `slot`, not on an arbitrary independent pane. The disposal effector reuses the slot-swap primitives on a non-slot pane.
- Suspect contributors: first_suppressed_viewer() picking a semantically-owned viewer; slot_pane reassignment when target wasn't the slot; geometry when the agent pane was stacked/sole content.

NOTE: not caused by the #N title change (that only alters the rename-pane string; suppress_pane is untouched). This is a pre-existing #207 defect that live-verify exposed — exactly step 8's purpose. disposed_reconciled_panes selector logic looks correct; the defect is in the suppress_pane EFFECTOR. Needs a fix + ideally a way to assert layout integrity. Operator cockpit left jumbled; recovering via `just refresh`.

the whole cockpit.

pane's exact place (open_command_pane_in_place_of_pane_id, geometry-
preserving), dropping the agent pane onto the suppressed stack without
touching the slot pool. One extra viewer process per disposal; the slot
rotation is left intact. Verified live: disposing a spawned agent now
swaps an empty Viewer into its tile with no layout jumble.

input.title: wait_for_idle can return on the boot-time settle before an agent's first turn
input.body:
Found during #208 live-verify (step 4). After spawn_agent with an opening prompt, the FIRST wait_for_idle([child]) can return {idle:true, settled:true} prematurely — it latches onto a brief idle/settle window during agent boot, BEFORE the queued opening input has been delivered+submitted and the agent has run its first turn. In the repro the child (#223) was told to note_append a result; wait_for_idle returned idle, but process_output showed the pane still "Orchestrating… (esc to interrupt)" and the note was empty. A second wait_for_idle returned idle again and by then the work was done.

Impact: orchestrators that do spawn_agent → wait_for_idle → read-result can read too early and see no result. Current robust workaround is wait-then-verify-the-artifact (re-read the agreed note/todo) or wait again.

Candidate fix: make wait_for_idle (or the settle/idle classifier) not report settled for an instance until its queued opening input has been delivered AND submitted — i.e. gate the first settle on input-queue drain / first observed thinking transition. Tag: agent-model. Related: #208.

input.title: Cockpit refresh orphans ephemeral ad-hoc agent configs (instances killed without process_delete)
input.body:
Found during #208 live-verify. Ephemeral ad-hoc configs (#205) are reaped only on process_delete of their LAST instance. A `just refresh` (or any cockpit teardown that kills agent panes/subprocesses without going through process_delete) leaves the instance rows as `exited` and their ephemeral configs orphaned in agent_tool_list — e.g. configs 222 (verify-result) and 228 (verify-ttl-sibling) lingered after a refresh killed instances #223/#229. Not a correctness bug in the #205 caller-driven model (reap is explicitly tied to process_delete), but it accumulates dead ephemeral configs across refreshes.

Candidate fixes (pick one): (a) a startup/boot sweep in the daemon that reaps ephemeral configs whose every instance is terminal (exited/stopped); (b) on cockpit boot, reconcile agent panes and process_delete instances whose panes no longer exist, which then cascades the existing last-instance reap; (c) leave as-is and document. Cleaned up the two this session created. Tag: agent-model. Related: #208, #205.

---
name: project-agent-cleanup-model
description: "Decided model for cleaning up spawned panopt agents (todo #190 line of work): caller-driven disposal + opt-in ephemeral TTL. A/B/C/D all DONE; live-verified under #208 (2026-06-08, all 8 steps pass) — which found+fixed a #207 pane-suppression layout-corruption bug."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b7f3f9f2-476c-4dfe-aed5-1a2198dc3bf8
---

Spawned agents persist (a config can fan out N instances since the 1:N factory change, todo #190). On 2026-06-07 the user chose the cleanup model: **caller-driven disposal + opt-in ephemeral TTL** (not pure-manual, not aggressive idle auto-reap — an idle-but-live Claude Code agent is expensive context and must NOT be auto-killed unless explicitly spawned ephemeral).

**Why:** matches soloterm's caller-driven discipline (stop_process vs close_process, no auto-reap) while adding a safety valve for one-shot fan-out. panopt's existing primitives: `process_stop` (→STOPPED, no resume — `process_start` now spawns fresh), `process_delete` (soft), `sweep_dead_processes` (running→EXITED on dead pid), `sweep_idle_agents` (prunes *registry* entry + locks at 30m, leaves the process row + pane). Never-close-panes invariant means disposal must *suppress* panes, not close them.

**How to apply (implementation status):**
- **A — disposal etiquette (DONE):** `spawn_agent` tool description + daemon server `instructions` (handler.rs get_info) say agents persist until disposed and to `process_stop` then `process_delete` what you spawn.
- **B — DONE (#205, e813b09):** schema V17 `ephemeral` col on `agent_tools`; ad-hoc `spawn_agent` sets it (via the post-create `agent_tool_update` patch, not a new create arg — kept the create signature to avoid churning ~20 test callers); `process_delete` → `reap_ephemeral_config` soft-deletes the config when its last live instance goes. Explicit/configured spawns stay durable.
- **C — DONE (#207, 9935faa):** plugin `reconcile_disposed_processes` (runs before the spawn reconciler prunes `reconciled_panes`) suppresses (never closes) the pane of any reconciled instance whose row is gone/terminal, via `suppress_pane` (reuse a suppressed viewer or `open_command_pane_in_place_of_pane_id` an empty one). Pure selector `disposed_reconciled_panes` is unit-tested.
- **D — DONE (#206, 70cb896):** schema V18 nullable `idle_ttl_secs` on *processes* (NOT a config flag — keyed off the per-instance TTL so auto-kill is strictly opt-in; the `ephemeral` flag is config-disposability only, a different axis). `SpawnAgentArgs.idle_ttl_secs` records it; daemon 15s timer runs `sweep_idle_ttl` (running + idle + ttl set + now-state_since≥ttl → process_stop+process_delete, returns pids; main.rs SIGTERMs them). Built D before C as planned.
- **Live verify all of it: #208** (needs `just refresh` outside Zellij; TUI I/O untestable in unit tests).

Related: [[rebuild-runtime-artifacts]] (must `just refresh` to test daemon/plugin changes).

---
name: project-agent-result-return
description: "How spawned sub-agent results return to the parent (agent-model work). Decided: full Solo parity — note/todo hand-off (docs done) + wait_for_idle + output-scrape tools (pending)."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b7f3f9f2-476c-4dfe-aed5-1a2198dc3bf8
---

`spawn_agent` returns a handle (`process_id`), not a future — results come back out-of-band, same as Solo. On 2026-06-07 the user chose **full Solo parity** for the three return mechanisms.

**Status / how to apply:**
- **#2 shared-state hand-off (DONE, works today):** notes (= Solo scratchpads) + todos + locks already exist. The pattern — agree a note/todo id up front, child writes result there before stopping, parent reads it — is now documented in the daemon server `instructions` (handler.rs get_info orchestration bullet) and the `[claude-code]` bootstrap `instructions` (defaults.toml: child writes its result to the named note/todo before finishing).
- **#3 synchronization (DONE) — `wait_for_idle`:** blocking `wait_for_idle(process_ids, timeout_ms, mode=all|any)` in handler.rs — async loop, takes the state Mutex only for the per-tick `process_get` snapshot and drops it before `tokio::sleep`. Settled = agent_state "idle" OR terminal status (stopped/exited) OR gone. Capped at 120s (default 60s); returns `{idle, timed_out, mode, processes:[{process_id,agent_state,status,settled}]}` so the parent re-calls on timeout. (Proxy `ureq` has no read timeout + daemon has no request-timeout layer, so the bounded block is safe.)
- **#1 PTY scrape (DONE) — `process_output`/`search_output`:** the plugin tees each running agent's viewport (last 300 rows) to `/host/.panopt/.cockpit/output-<id>.txt` in `observe_agent_states` (`write_output_capture`); core `Store::process_output`/`search_output` read `<root>/.panopt/.cockpit/output-<id>.txt` (tail-by-lines / substring). Laggy ~1s, window-only — brittle; notes preferred.

All wired through TOOL_SURFACE + Tool enum + dispatch_local (covered by handler::tests::tool_enum_covers_tool_surface). Verified by build/clippy/tests; **live verification still needed** (spawn a child, wait_for_idle, read its note; process_output after `just refresh`). Related: [[project-agent-cleanup-model]], [[rebuild-runtime-artifacts]].

`spawn_agent` returns a handle (`process_id`), not a future — results come back out-of-band, same as Solo. On 2026-06-07 the user chose **full Solo parity** for the three return mechanisms.

**Status / how to apply:**
- **#2 shared-state hand-off (DONE, works today):** notes (= Solo scratchpads) + todos + locks already exist. The pattern — agree a note/todo id up front, child writes result there before stopping, parent reads it — is now documented in the daemon server `instructions` (handler.rs get_info orchestration bullet) and the `[claude-code]` bootstrap `instructions` (defaults.toml: child writes its result to the named note/todo before finishing).
- **#3 synchronization (DONE) — `wait_for_idle`:** blocking `wait_for_idle(process_ids, timeout_ms, mode=all|any)` in handler.rs — async loop, takes the state Mutex only for the per-tick `process_get` snapshot and drops it before `tokio::sleep`. Settled = agent_state "idle" OR terminal status (stopped/exited) OR gone. Capped at 120s (default 60s); returns `{idle, timed_out, mode, processes:[{process_id,agent_state,status,settled}]}` so the parent re-calls on timeout. (Proxy `ureq` has no read timeout + daemon has no request-timeout layer, so the bounded block is safe.)

Confirmed by reading all the paths. **No — handing an agent-management tool a todo's id cannot delete the todo.** Two independent guarantees:

**1. Every agent-mgmt delete is scoped to its own table by `(project_id, id)`** — a todo id matches nothing, so you get a not-found error or no-op, never a todo touch:

| Tool | Core query | Given a todo's id (e.g. 10) |
|------|-----------|------------------------------|
| `process_delete` | `UPDATE processes … WHERE id=?` | 0 rows → `ProcessNotFound` error |
| `process_stop` | `fetch_process(id)` first | not found → error, nothing mutated |
| `agent_tool_delete` | `UPDATE agent_tools … WHERE id=?` | 0 rows → `AgentToolNotFound` error |
| `reap_ephemeral_config` | `UPDATE agent_tools … WHERE id=?`, gated on `ephemeral=1` | only ever runs on a config id from a just-deleted process |

Because the id counter is shared, id 10 resolves to **exactly one** resource — in twopic it's a todo, and *no* process or config has id 10 — so `process_delete(10)`/`agent_tool_delete(10)` there simply find nothing.

**2. The decisive one: `todos.deleted_at` has exactly one writer in the entire core** — line 1985, inside `todo_delete`. No process path, no config path, no reap, no sweep writes the todos table at all. So a todo can *only* be soft-deleted by the `todo_delete` MCP tool.

**Therefore twopic #10 was a genuine `todo_delete(#10)` call** — not an agent-management tool misfiring on a stray id. The id-sharing is type-safe by construction here; the cross-resource-deletion theory is closed off.

(If you want runtime proof rather than code proof, I can demo in one of the `/tmp/panopt-test` scratch projects: call `process_delete` with a todo's id and show it errors with the todo left intact. Say the word.)

## Summary Report: PANopt TODO Status Model and Blocker/Dependency System

I've thoroughly explored the panopt repository and mapped the TODO status model and blocker system. Here are my findings:

---

### 1. **Set of Allowed TODO Status Values**

**Files:**
- `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-core/src/model.rs:84-119` (enum definition)
- `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-core/src/db.rs:54-64` (V2 schema migration)
- `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-tool-surface/src/params.rs:99-180` (TodoCreateArgs/TodoUpdateArgs)
- `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panoptd/src/handler.rs:617-621` (parse_status function)

**Status Model:**
Status is **an enum, NOT free-form text**. The `TodoStatus` enum in `model.rs:84-91` defines exactly six values:
```rust
pub enum TodoStatus {
    #[default]
    Open,
    InProgress,
    Backlog,
    Draft,
    Completed,
    NotDone,
}
```

**Allowed Status Strings** (wire/storage format):
- `"open"` (default)
- `"in_progress"`
- `"backlog"`
- `"draft"`
- `"completed"`
- `"not_done"`

**Validation:**
The status is stored as TEXT in the `todos.status` column, but parsing is strict. Two functions validate it:
1. `TodoStatus::parse(s: &str) -> Option<TodoStatus>` (model.rs:108-118) — returns `None` for unrecognized strings
2. `parse_status(s: &str) -> Result<TodoStatus, McpError>` (handler.rs:617-621) — in panoptd, returns a typed error with a caller-facing message listing the six valid values

The only undocumented status mutation during migrations was in V2 (db.rs:64), where legacy `'done'` was rewritten to `'completed'`:
```sql
UPDATE todos SET status = 'completed' WHERE status = 'done';
```

---

### 2. **Blocker Model and Dependency Resolution**

**Schema:**
- Table: `todo_blockers` (db.rs:79-89, SCHEMA_V2)
```sql
CREATE TABLE todo_blockers (
    project_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    todo_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    blocker_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (project_id, todo_id, blocker_id),
    CHECK (todo_id != blocker_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (project_id, todo_id)
        REFERENCES todos(project_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    FOREIGN KEY (project_id, blocker_id)
        REFERENCES todos(project_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
```

**Functions:**
- `todo_add_blocker(project, id, blocker_id)` (state.rs:1997-2015) — adds a row to `todo_blockers`, idempotent
- `todo_remove_blocker(project, id, blocker_id)` (state.rs:2019-2033) — deletes from `todo_blockers`, idempotent
- `todo_set_blockers(project, id, blockers: Vec<u64>)` (state.rs:2127-2161) — atomic replacement, diffs the desired set
- `todo_blockers(project, id) -> Vec<u64>` (state.rs:2269-2285) — fetch list of blocker ids, filtering out soft-deleted blockers

**Blocker Representation:**
In the `Todo` struct (model.rs:168-188):
```rust
pub blockers: Vec<u64>,  // Ids of other todos in the same project that block this one.
```

**CRITICAL: No Computed "Ready" or "Blocked" State**

I searched exhaustively for any logic that computes "all dependencies satisfied" or derived states like "Ready" or "Blocked". **None exists.** The system stores blockers (the raw dependency edges) but does NOT compute:
- Whether a todo is "ready" (open + all blockers completed)
- Whether a todo is "blocked" (open + any blocker incomplete)
- Any transitive dependency satisfaction

This is completely absent from:
- `Store::fetch_todo` and related reads
- `Store::todo_*` methods
- Projection code
- MCP tool surface (todo_list, todo_get return blocker ids verbatim, no computed state)

The blocker query in `todo_blockers()` simply fetches the ids of non-soft-deleted blockers. It does NOT check blocker status.

---

### 3. **Status and Blocker Info in Projection**

**Todo Index Format** (`render_todos_index_md`, projection.rs:140-165):
```
- [{mark}] [#{id}](todos/{id}.md) {title} - {status}, {priority}, updated {updated}\n
```
Where `mark` is `'x'` for Completed, `'-'` for NotDone, `' '` (space) for all others.

**Example output:**
```
- [x] [#1](todos/1.md) Done thing - completed, high, updated 2026-06-08 10:30:00
- [ ] [#2](todos/2.md) Open task - open, medium, updated 2026-06-08 09:15:00
```

**Status and blocker info are NOT in the index line.** The status is shown textually, but blockers are not rendered here.

**Per-Todo File Format** (`render_todo_md`, projection.rs:167-196):
```yaml
---
status: {status}
priority: {priority}
assignee: {assignee}
tags: {tag1, tag2, ...}
blockers: {blocker_id1}, {blocker_id2}, ...
created: {timestamp}
updated: {timestamp}
completed: {timestamp}  // only if status is Completed
---

# {title}

{body}

## Comments
{comments}
```

**Example:**
```yaml
---
status: open
priority: medium
assignee: greg
tags: feature, urgent
blockers: 3, 7
created: 2026-06-08 08:00:00
updated: 2026-06-08 10:30:00
---

# Implement color coding
...
```

Blockers are a comma-separated list of ids in the frontmatter. The projection includes the raw blocker id list, NOT any derived "Ready" or "Blocked" state.

---

### 4. **Schema Migrations (V1–V18, currently at V18)**

**Current Version:** V18 (db.rs:18)

**Latest Changes Relevant to Todos:**
- **V2** (db.rs:47-90): Initial todo data model with `status` TEXT column, plus `todo_blockers` and `todo_comments` side tables
- **V7** (db.rs:333-346): Added soft-delete via `deleted_at` column to todos
- **V18** (db.rs:575-587): Added `idle_ttl_secs` to processes (unrelated to todos)

**Forward Migration Pattern:**
All migrations are forward-only:
1. Add a new `fn apply_v<n>(conn: &Connection)` function in `db.rs`
2. Add an `if version < n { apply_v<n>(conn)?; }` step in the `migrate()` function
3. Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = n` at the top of `db.rs`
4. Use `add_column_if_missing()` for column additions to handle dev-database drift (transitional state where a column landed before its `user_version` bump)

**To Add a New Status Value:**
Since status is validated in Rust via the `TodoStatus` enum, adding a new status requires:
1. New enum variant in `model.rs:84-92`
2. New case in `TodoStatus::as_str()` (model.rs:96-105)
3. New case in `TodoStatus::parse()` (model.rs:108-118)
4. Updated handler validation in `handler.rs:617-621` (the error message listing valid values)
5. Updated docs in `params.rs:105-106` and `lib.rs:207-209` (TOOL_SURFACE description)
6. **NO database migration needed** — the `status` column remains TEXT, the Rust parsing is the validation layer

**To Add a New Stored Column** (e.g., `waiting_external`, `needs_review` as enum-like statuses, or new metadata):
1. New `apply_v<n>()` function using `add_column_if_missing()` with `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` for backward compatibility
2. Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`
3. If it's another status-like field (not a variant of the main `status` enum), add a new enum type (like `TodoStatus`) or keep it TEXT — either way, add Rust parsing and validation
4. Update projection to render it

---

### 5. **MCP Tool Surface for Todos**

**Files:**
- `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-tool-surface/src/lib.rs:69-468` (TOOL_SURFACE table)
- `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-tool-surface/src/params.rs` (argument types)
- `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panoptd/src/handler.rs` (implementations)

**Relevant Tool Definitions in TOOL_SURFACE:**

| Tool | Description | Accepts Status | Returns Status/Blockers |
|------|-------------|---|---|
| `todo_create` (lib.rs:172-178) | Create a new todo | Optional `status` field (one of open/in_progress/backlog/draft/completed/not_done) | Returns id |
| `todo_list` (lib.rs:180-185) | List all todos | N/A | Returns `{id, title, status, priority, assignee, tags, blockers, comment_count, created_at, updated_at}` |
| `todo_search` (lib.rs:187-195) | Find todos | Optional `status` filter | Same as todo_list |
| `todo_get` (lib.rs:197-202) | Fetch one todo in full | N/A | Full todo with body, comments, blockers, `locked_by` |
| `todo_update` (lib.rs:204-210) | Edit a todo | Optional `status` field | N/A (mutation only) |
| `todo_complete` (lib.rs:212-215) | Mark complete | N/A | N/A |
| `todo_start` (lib.rs:217-227) | Claim for work (acquire lock + set to in_progress) | N/A (only transitions to in_progress) | Full todo |
| `todo_add_blocker` (lib.rs:235-239) | Add a blocker link | N/A | N/A |
| `todo_remove_blocker` (lib.rs:241-245) | Remove a blocker link | N/A | N/A |
| `todo_set_blockers` (lib.rs:266-271) | Atomic blocker replacement | N/A | N/A |

**Status Acceptance in TodoCreateArgs** (params.rs:99-118):
```rust
/// Initial status: one of open, in_progress, backlog, draft, completed,
/// not_done. Omit to default to open.
#[serde(default)]
pub status: Option<String>,
```

**Status Acceptance in TodoUpdateArgs** (params.rs:154-180):
```rust
/// New status: one of open, in_progress, backlog, draft, completed,
/// not_done. Omit to leave unchanged.
#[serde(default)]
pub status: Option<String>,
```

**Wire Format for Blockers:**
The `todo_blockers` table in MCP responses is returned as a simple array of ids (see `todo_list` output shape in lib.rs:182-184). No computed derived state is returned.

---

1. **Status values are fixed at 6** and validated in Rust. New enum-like states require adding an enum variant + parse/render code, not just a new status string.

2. **Blockers exist but are not resolved.** There's no "Ready" or "Blocked" state computed from the blocker graph. To add derived states like:
   - `Ready` = `status == open` AND all blockers are `completed`
   - `Blocked` = `status == open` AND any blocker is NOT `completed`

   - Compute these in the projection layer when rendering the index/per-todo files
   - Optionally expose them as read-only fields in `todo_list`/`todo_get` output (added to the wire shape in `handler.rs`, not stored in the database)
   - The blocker resolution logic would live in Rust code, not SQL

   - A new V19 migration adding a nullable TEXT column (or keep them as status enum variants)
   - Parsing + validation in Rust
   - Updates to TOOL_SURFACE documentation and TodoCreateArgs/TodoUpdateArgs

4. **Projection changes** needed:
   - Update `render_todos_index_md` to add derived state rendering (e.g., `[!]` for blocked, `[→]` for ready)
   - Update `render_todo_md` to include derived state in the frontmatter (computed at render time, not stored)

| Projection (index) | `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-core/src/projection.rs:140-165` |
| Projection (per-todo) | `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-core/src/projection.rs:167-196` |
| Migrations | `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-core/src/db.rs:18` (SCHEMA_VERSION) + `migrate()` function |
| TOOL_SURFACE | `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-tool-surface/src/lib.rs:69-468` |

# Implementation Plan: panopt #236 "color code todos"

## Verified findings (reconciling the brief)

1. **No existing blocker-aware filter exists anywhere.** `handler.rs::todo_search` (handler.rs:1000-1032) and `todo_list` call `st.todo_search`/`st.todo_list` with no blocker/ready computation. The MCP/tool-surface layer has no "is blocked" or "unblocked" logic — only the raw blocker CRUD (`todo_add_blocker`, etc.). The comment at `zellij-logic/src/lib.rs:108-113` claiming "the viewer pane on the right uses MCP and applies the full blocker-aware filter" is **aspirational, not real**. There is nothing to reuse. The canonical `is_blocked` must be created fresh, and it belongs in **core**.

2. **Core projection already has every todo's status at render time.** `state.rs::reproject_todos` (state.rs:2319-2321) calls `project_todos(root, &self.todo_list(project)?)` with the *full* project todo list on every mutation. `project_todos` (projection.rs:511-516) passes that whole slice to `render_todos_index_md` (projection.rs:140-165). So the index renderer can build an id→status map and resolve each row's blockers to their statuses — no DB change, no new query. And because *any* status change reprojects the whole list, a blocker flipping to `completed` automatically re-renders the blocked row. This is the linchpin: **blocked-state is computed at index-render time in core and stamped into the index line.**

3. **`Todo.blockers: Vec<u64>`** (model.rs:181) is populated on every `todo_get`/`todo_list`, so it's present in the slice.

---

## Part A — MUST-HAVE: color existing statuses + Ready/Blocked (green/red)

### Step A1 — Canonical `is_blocked` in core (model.rs)

Add to `crates/panopt-core/src/model.rs`, a free function (testable, no I/O):

```rust
/// A todo is *blocked* when it is actionable (Open) yet at least one of its
/// blockers is not yet terminal-done. `statuses_by_id` maps every todo id in
/// the project to its status; a blocker id missing from the map (soft-deleted
/// or dangling) is treated as resolved, matching `todo_blockers()` which only
/// returns live blockers.
pub fn is_blocked(todo: &Todo, statuses_by_id: &HashMap<u64, TodoStatus>) -> bool {
    if todo.status != TodoStatus::Open { return false; }
    todo.blockers.iter().any(|b| {
        matches!(statuses_by_id.get(b), Some(s) if !s.is_done())
    })
}
```

Add a helper `TodoStatus::is_done(self) -> bool` returning `matches!(self, Completed | NotDone)` (a `NotDone` blocker is closed → no longer blocking; this matches the existing `[-]` "cancelled/won't-do" semantics in projection.rs:149-153). Document the choice in the doc comment.

**Decision recorded:** "ready/blocked" is *derived*, never stored. Only `Open` todos can be Ready or Blocked. `is_blocked` is the single source of truth, lives in core, and is unit-tested there.

### Step A2 — A derived `TodoRowState` enum + color mapping in zellij-logic

The *color* decision is presentation, so it lives in `crates/panopt-zellij-logic/src/lib.rs` where it's unit-testable without the WASM/Zellij host:

```rust
/// The visual state a Todos-pane row is painted in. Derived from the stored
/// status plus the projection's per-row blocked flag (todo #236); never stored.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum TodoRowState {
    Completed,   // gray
    InProgress,  // blue
    Blocked,     // red   (open + a blocker not done)
    Ready,       // green (open + all blockers done / none)
    NotDone,     // dark gray
    Other,       // backlog/draft → default fg
}

impl TodoRowState {
    /// 256-color foreground code, or None for terminal default.
    pub fn fg_code(self) -> Option<u8> {
        match self {
            TodoRowState::Completed => Some(245), // gray
            TodoRowState::InProgress => Some(39),  // blue
            TodoRowState::Blocked => Some(160),    // red
            TodoRowState::Ready => Some(34),       // green
            TodoRowState::NotDone => Some(240),    // dark gray
            TodoRowState::Other => None,
        }
    }
}
```

Plus a pure classifier driven by the projection label (status token + the new blocked flag):

```rust
/// Classify a projection-index label into its paint state. `status` comes
/// from `parse_status_suffix`; `blocked` from `parse_blocked_suffix` (#236).
pub fn row_state_for(label: &str) -> TodoRowState { ... }
```

**Precedence** (from the todo, minus the optional new states for now): completed → in_progress → blocked(open) → ready(open) → not_done → other. Encode this precedence explicitly in `row_state_for`.

### Step A3 — Index line format change (the back-compat-sensitive commit)

This is the one change that **must touch the core writer and the zellij-logic reader in the same commit** so the tree stays buildable and the reader tolerates both shapes.

**Before** (projection.rs:155-162):
```
- [ ] [#7](todos/7.md) wire up auth - open, high, updated 2026-05-23 18:05:21
```

**After** — append a blocked marker only for blocked rows, as a new comma-token in the existing suffix so all existing parsers keep working:
```
- [ ] [#7](todos/7.md) wire up auth - open, high, updated 2026-05-23 18:05:21, blocked
```

Design rationale for *this* shape:
- It is **append-only** in the comma-list, exactly like the `updated <ts>` token was added before it (see parse_updated_suffix's note at lib.rs:257-261). Existing `parse_status_suffix` (slices token *before first comma*) and `parse_priority_suffix` (slices *second* token) and `parse_updated_suffix` (scans for `updated ` prefix) are all unaffected.
- Only *blocked* (`Open` + unresolved blocker) rows get the token. Ready rows get nothing → an older reader simply sees plain `open` and degrades to today's behavior (green is the "normal" open state anyway). This keeps the marker rare and the diff small.

Implementation in `render_todos_index_md`:
- Change signature is *not* needed externally — build the map internally:
  ```rust
  let statuses: HashMap<u64, TodoStatus> =
      todos.iter().map(|t| (t.id, t.status)).collect();
  ```
- In the loop, `if is_blocked(todo, &statuses) { push ", blocked" }` after the `updated ...` segment.

Reader side, in zellij-logic, add:
```rust
/// True when the projection-index label carries the `, blocked` marker (#236).
pub fn parse_blocked_suffix(label: &str) -> bool {
    suffix_start(label)
        .map(|s| label[s..].split(',').map(str::trim).any(|t| t == "blocked"))
        .unwrap_or(false)
}
```
Then `row_state_for(label)` uses `parse_status_suffix` + `parse_blocked_suffix`.

**Commit boundary:** A3's writer change + the `parse_blocked_suffix`/`row_state_for`/`TodoRowState` reader additions land together. No painting yet — both sides compile and `cargo test` passes with new unit tests on the round-trip.

### Step A4 — Thread state into the plugin `Item` and extend `paint()`

In `crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs`:

1. **`Item` struct** (main.rs:331-337): add `state: Option<TodoRowState>` (None for non-todo modes). Set it only in the Todos branch of `rebuild_items` (main.rs:1358-1364):
   ```rust

       label: format!("#{id} {label}"),
       target: ItemTarget::Todo(*id),
       live: false,
       state: Some(panopt_zellij_logic::row_state_for(label)),
   })
   ```
   Other branches set `state: None`.

2. **`Style` enum** (main.rs:3135-3139): replace the bare `Normal`/`Dim` with a variant carrying an optional fg color, or add `Style::Fg(u8)`. Minimal approach — add a field rather than a combinatorial enum:
   - Change `paint(content, cols, style, focused)` → `paint(content, cols, style, fg: Option<u8>, focused)`.
   - In `paint` (main.rs:3144-3159), after the existing `7`/`2` codes, push the fg: `if let Some(c) = fg { codes.push(&format!("38;5;{c}")) }` (build into an owned `String` vec to satisfy lifetimes).

3. **Render loop** (main.rs:672-683): pass `item.state.and_then(TodoRowState::fg_code)` as the `fg` arg. All other `paint(...)` call sites (help lines 664, none-line 670, status line 692) pass `None`.

**Focus interaction risk + decision:** the focused row uses SGR `7` (reverse), which swaps fg/bg. A green fg under reverse becomes a green *background*, which is fine and still distinguishes state, but verify it's legible. If not, the fallback is to suppress fg when `focused` (cursor row stays plain reverse). Recommend keeping color under reverse and confirming visually in Step C.

---

## Part B — OPTIONAL add-on: new stored states (waiting / needs_review / canceled)

Cleanly separable; do **not** block Part A on it. Each new state is a stored status, so it's the full enum-variant ritual. Ordered, and each item is one coordinated commit:

7. **docs** — DESIGN.md status enum section, any CLAUDE.md status list.

- `is_blocked`: open+incomplete-blocker → true; open+all-completed-blockers → false; open+no-blockers → false; in_progress/completed/backlog → false regardless; blocker id missing from map → treated resolved; `NotDone`/`Canceled` blocker → not blocking.
- `render_todos_index_md` round-trip: a project with a blocked row emits `, blocked`; a ready row does not; assert exact line text (before/after strings above).

**zellij-logic (`cargo test -p panopt-zellij-logic`):**
- `parse_blocked_suffix`: true for `... updated <ts>, blocked`; false for plain row; false for label with no suffix; tolerant of empty-title `- open, high, blocked`.
- `row_state_for` precedence table: one assertion per state, including completed-beats-blocked and in_progress-beats-blocked.
- Back-compat: a pre-#236 label (no `blocked` token) classifies open→Ready and never panics; `parse_status_suffix`/`parse_priority_suffix`/`parse_updated_suffix` still return the same values when `, blocked` is appended.

**plugin (`cargo test -p panopt-zellij`, runs on host):**
- `paint` with `fg: Some(34)` emits `\u{1b}[38;5;34m`; with focus emits `7;38;5;34`; with `None` is unchanged from today (guards the existing snapshot-style tests at main.rs:3161+).

## End-to-end verification

1. `cargo test` workspace-wide, plus the WASM build — run the **verify-all** skill (it does the workspace + `wasm32-wasip1` panopt-zellij dance).
2. Manual: in a project with todos where #A blocks #B (both open), `just refresh` (rebuild + reload plugin), open the Todos pane. Expect: #B red (Blocked), #A green (Ready), an in_progress todo blue, a completed todo gray. Complete #A → reproject fires → #B flips green. /// blockers is not yet terminal-done. `statuses_by_id` maps every todo id in
/// the project to its status; a blocker id missing from the map (soft-deleted
/// or dangling) is treated as resolved, matching `todo_blockers()` which only
/// returns live blockers.
pub fn is_blocked(todo: &Todo, statuses_by_id: &HashMap<u64, TodoStatus>) -> bool {
    if todo.status != TodoStatus::Open { return false; }
    todo.blockers.iter().any(|b| {
        matches!(statuses_by_id.get(b), Some(s) if !s.is_done())
    })
}
```

Add a helper `TodoStatus::is_done(self) -> bool` returning `matches!(self, Completed | NotDone)` (a `NotDone` blocker is closed → no longer blocking; this matches the existing `[-]` "cancelled/won't-do" semantics in projection.rs:149-153). Document the choice in the doc comment.

**Decision recorded:** "ready/blocked" is *derived*, never stored. Only `Open` todos can be Ready or Blocked. `is_blocked` is the single source of truth, lives in core, and is unit-tested there.

### Step A2 — A derived `TodoRowState` enum + color mapping in zellij-logic

The *color* decision is presentation, so it lives in `crates/panopt-zellij-logic/src/lib.rs` where it's unit-testable without the WASM/Zellij host:

```rust
/// The visual state a Todos-pane row is painted in. Derived from the stored
/// status plus the projection's per-row blocked flag (todo #236); never stored.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum TodoRowState {
    Completed,   // gray
    InProgress,  // blue
    Blocked,     // red   (open + a blocker not done)
    Ready,       // green (open + all blockers done / none)
    NotDone,     // dark gray
    Other,       // backlog/draft → default fg
}

impl TodoRowState {
    /// 256-color foreground code, or None for terminal default.
    pub fn fg_code(self) -> Option<u8> {
        match self {
            TodoRowState::Completed => Some(245), // gray
            TodoRowState::InProgress => Some(39),  // blue
            TodoRowState::Blocked => Some(160),    // red
            TodoRowState::Ready => Some(34),       // green
            TodoRowState::NotDone => Some(240),    // dark gray
            TodoRowState::Other => None,
        }
    }
}
```

Plus a pure classifier driven by the projection label (status token + the new blocked flag):

```rust
/// Classify a projection-index label into its paint state. `status` comes
/// from `parse_status_suffix`; `blocked` from `parse_blocked_suffix` (#236).
pub fn row_state_for(label: &str) -> TodoRowState { ... }
```

**Precedence** (from the todo, minus the optional new states for now): completed → in_progress → blocked(open) → ready(open) → not_done → other. Encode this precedence explicitly in `row_state_for`.

### Step A3 — Index line format change (the back-compat-sensitive commit)

This is the one change that **must touch the core writer and the zellij-logic reader in the same commit** so the tree stays buildable and the reader tolerates both shapes.

**Before** (projection.rs:155-162):
```
- [ ] [#7](todos/7.md) wire up auth - open, high, updated 2026-05-23 18:05:21
```

**After** — append a blocked marker only for blocked rows, as a new comma-token in the existing suffix so all existing parsers keep working:
```
- [ ] [#7](todos/7.md) wire up auth - open, high, updated 2026-05-23 18:05:21, blocked
```

Design rationale for *this* shape:
- It is **append-only** in the comma-list, exactly like the `updated <ts>` token was added before it (see parse_updated_suffix's note at lib.rs:257-261). Existing `parse_status_suffix` (slices token *before first comma*) and `parse_priority_suffix` (slices *second* token) and `parse_updated_suffix` (scans for `updated ` prefix) are all unaffected.
- Only *blocked* (`Open` + unresolved blocker) rows get the token. Ready rows get nothing → an older reader simply sees plain `open` and degrades to today's behavior (green is the "normal" open state anyway). This keeps the marker rare and the diff small.
- A stale on-disk index (pre-#236) has no `blocked` token → every open row classifies as Ready. Acceptable degradation; the next daemon mutation reprojects with the real flag.

Implementation in `render_todos_index_md`:
- Change signature is *not* needed externally — build the map internally:
  ```rust
  let statuses: HashMap<u64, TodoStatus> =
      todos.iter().map(|t| (t.id, t.status)).collect();
  ```
- In the loop, `if is_blocked(todo, &statuses) { push ", blocked" }` after the `updated ...` segment.

Reader side, in zellij-logic, add:
```rust
/// True when the projection-index label carries the `, blocked` marker (#236).
pub fn parse_blocked_suffix(label: &str) -> bool {
    suffix_start(label)
        .map(|s| label[s..].split(',').map(str::trim).any(|t| t == "blocked"))
        .unwrap_or(false)
}
```
Then `row_state_for(label)` uses `parse_status_suffix` + `parse_blocked_suffix`.

**Commit boundary:** A3's writer change + the `parse_blocked_suffix`/`row_state_for`/`TodoRowState` reader additions land together. No painting yet — both sides compile and `cargo test` passes with new unit tests on the round-trip.

# Plan: color-code todos (#236)

## Context

Todo #236 wants the Zellij sidebar's Todos pane to color-code rows by a derived
state so the list is "immediately useful" at a glance — the headline being a
**green = Ready (open, all dependencies done)** vs **red = Blocked (open, a
dependency still incomplete)** split, plus per-status colors. Today every row is
plain text; status is only conveyed as a `- open, high, updated …` text suffix,
and the sidebar literally *cannot* tell ready from blocked because the projection
index it reads (`/host/.panopt/todos.md`) carries no blocker information
(documented as a known gap at `zellij-logic/src/lib.rs:108-113`).

Two prerequisites were settled with the user:
- **Scope = full 7-state model.** Of the todo's 7 states, `completed`(gray),
  `in_progress`(blue), and `canceled/obsolete`(dark gray) already exist —
  `canceled` maps onto the existing `not_done` status, which projection.rs
  already documents as the "cancelled / won't-do" state. Ready/Blocked are
  *derived* from `open` + blockers. Only **`waiting`(amber)** and
  **`needs_review`(purple)** are genuinely new stored statuses, and we are
  adding them.
- **Ready rule:** green only for `open` + *all* blockers done, where a blocker
  counts as done if its status is `completed` OR `not_done` (a closed blocker no
  longer blocks). Red otherwise.

No DB migration is needed: status stays a TEXT column validated by the Rust
`TodoStatus` enum, and ready/blocked is derived at projection-render time (never
stored).

## Branch

Create a topic branch off `main` (the documented PR base; keeps #236 independent
of the in-flight `agent-model` work):

```
git checkout main && git checkout -b todo-236-color-code-todos
```

## Color reference (256-color SGR `38;5;N`)

| State | Source | Code |
|-------|--------|------|
| Ready | `open` + all blockers done | green `34` |
| Blocked | `open` + a blocker not done | red `160` |
| In progress | `in_progress` | blue `39` |
| Needs review | `needs_review` (new) | purple `99` |
| Waiting | `waiting` (new) | amber `214` |
| Completed | `completed` | gray `245` |
| Canceled/obsolete | `not_done` | dark gray `240` |
| Backlog / draft | `backlog`,`draft` | terminal default (no code) |

## Implementation (ordered; each commit builds + tests green)

### Commit 1 — core: derived blocked-state + projection marker
`crates/panopt-core/src/model.rs`
- Add `TodoStatus::is_done(self) -> bool` → `matches!(self, Completed | NotDone)`
  (and `Canceled` once added — same idea). Doc *why*: a closed blocker no longer
  blocks.
- Add free fn `is_blocked(todo: &Todo, statuses_by_id: &HashMap<u64, TodoStatus>) -> bool`:
  `todo.status == Open && todo.blockers.iter().any(|b| matches!(statuses_by_id.get(b), Some(s) if !s.is_done()))`.
  A blocker id absent from the map (soft-deleted/dangling) is treated resolved,
  matching `todo_blockers()` which only returns live blockers.

`crates/panopt-core/src/projection.rs` — `render_todos_index_md` (138-165)
- Build `let statuses: HashMap<u64, TodoStatus> = todos.iter().map(|t| (t.id, t.status)).collect();`
  (the slice already carries `.blockers`, see `render_todo_md`).
- Append `, blocked` to the line **only when** `is_blocked(todo, &statuses)`, after
  the `updated {updated}` token. Before/after:
  ```
  - [ ] [#7](todos/7.md) wire up auth - open, high, updated 2026-05-23 18:05:21
  - [ ] [#7](todos/7.md) wire up auth - open, high, updated 2026-05-23 18:05:21, blocked
  ```
  Append-only: existing readers slice the 1st/2nd comma-token and the
  `updated `-prefixed token (`parse_status_suffix`/`parse_priority_suffix`/
  `parse_updated_suffix`), all inert to a trailing `, blocked`.
- Reproject already fires on every todo mutation (`reproject_todos` →
  `project_todos` → `render_todos_index_md`), so completing a blocker

  counts as done if its status is `completed` OR `not_done` (a closed blocker no
  longer blocks). Red otherwise.

stored).

| Blocked | `open` + a blocker not done | red `160` |
| In progress | `in_progress` | blue `39` |
| Needs review | `needs_review` (new) | purple `99` |
| Waiting | `waiting` (new) | amber `214` |
| Completed | `completed` | gray `245` |

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: color-code todos (#236)

## Context

Todo #236 wants the Zellij sidebar's Todos pane to color-code rows by a derived
state so the list is "immediately useful" at a glance — the headline being a
**green = Ready (open, all dependencies done)** vs **red = Blocked (open, a
dependency still incomplete)** split, plus per-status colors. Today every row is
plain text; status is only conveyed as a `- open, high, updated …` text suffix,
and the sidebar literally *cannot* tell ready from blocked because the projection
index it reads (`/host/.panopt/todos.md`) carries no blocker information
(documented as a known gap at `zellij-logic/src/lib.rs:108-113`).

Two prerequisites were settled with the user:
- **Scope = full 7-state model.** Of the todo's 7 states, `completed`(gray),
  `in_progress`(blue), and `canceled/obsolete`(dark gray) already exist —
  `canceled` maps onto the existing `not_done` status, which projection.rs
  already documents as the "cancelled / won't-do" state. Ready/Blocked are
  *derived* from `open` + blockers. Only **`waiting`(amber)** and
  **`needs_review`(purple)** are genuinely new stored statuses, and we are
  adding them.
- **Ready rule:** green only for `open` + *all* blockers done, where a blocker
  counts as done if its status is `completed` OR `not_done` (a closed blocker no
  longer blocks). Red otherwise.

No DB migration is needed: status stays a TEXT column validated by the Rust
`TodoStatus` enum, and ready/blocked is derived at projection-render time (never
stored).

## Branch

Create a topic branch off `main` (the documented PR base; keeps #236 independent
of the in-flight `agent-model` work):

```
git checkout main && git checkout -b todo-236-color-code-todos
```

## Color reference (256-color SGR `38;5;N`)

| State | Source | Code |
|-------|--------|------|
| Ready | `open` + all blockers done | green `34` |
| Blocked | `open` + a blocker not done | red `160` |
| In progress | `in_progress` | blue `39` |
| Needs review | `needs_review` (new) | purple `99` |
| Waiting | `waiting` (new) | amber `214` |
| Completed | `completed` | gray `245` |
| Canceled/obsolete | `not_done` | dark gray `240` |
| Backlog / draft | `backlog`,`draft` | terminal default (no code) |

## Implementation (ordered; each commit builds + tests green)

### Commit 1 — core: derived blocked-state + projection marker
`crates/panopt-core/src/model.rs`
- Add `TodoStatus::is_done(self) -> bool` → `matches!(self, Completed | NotDone)`
  (and `Canceled` once added — same idea). Doc *why*: a closed blocker no longer
  blocks.
- Add free fn `is_blocked(todo: &Todo, statuses_by_id: &HashMap<u64, TodoStatus>) -> bool`:
  `todo.status == Open && todo.blockers.iter().any(|b| matches!(statuses_by_id.get(b), Some(s) if !s.is_done()))`.
  A blocker id absent from the map (soft-deleted/dangling) is treated resolved,
  matching `todo_blockers()` which only returns live blockers.

`crates/panopt-core/src/projection.rs` — `render_todos_index_md` (138-165)
- Build `let statuses: HashMap<u64, TodoStatus> = todos.iter().map(|t| (t.id, t.status)).collect();`
  (the slice already carries `.blockers`, see `render_todo_md`).
- Append `, blocked` to the line **only when** `is_blocked(todo, &statuses)`, after
  the `updated {updated}` token. Before/after:
  ```
  - [ ] [#7](todos/7.md) wire up auth - open, high, updated 2026-05-23 18:05:21
  - [ ] [#7](todos/7.md) wire up auth - open, high, updated 2026-05-23 18:05:21, blocked
  ```
  Append-only: existing readers slice the 1st/2nd comma-token and the
  `updated `-prefixed token (`parse_status_suffix`/`parse_priority_suffix`/
  `parse_updated_suffix`), all inert to a trailing `, blocked`.
- Reproject already fires on every todo mutation (`reproject_todos` →
  `project_todos` → `render_todos_index_md`), so completing a blocker
  automatically re-renders the dependent row's flag — no extra plumbing.

Tests (`cargo test -p panopt-core`): `is_blocked` truth table (open+incomplete→true;
open+all-done→false; open+no-blockers→false; non-open→false; missing blocker→resolved;
`not_done` blocker→not blocking) and a `render_todos_index_md` assertion that a
blocked row emits `, blocked` and a ready row does not.

### Commit 2 — zellij-logic: parse the marker + state→color (with new statuses)
`crates/panopt-zellij-logic/src/lib.rs`
- `parse_blocked_suffix(label) -> bool`: `suffix_start(label)` then any comma-token
  trims to `"blocked"`. Parallel to `parse_updated_suffix`.
- Extend `parse_status_suffix`'s allow-list (235-239) with `"waiting"` and
  `"needs_review"`.
- Add `enum TodoRowState { Ready, Blocked, InProgress, Waiting, NeedsReview, Completed, Canceled, Other }`
  with `fn fg_code(self) -> Option<u8>` per the color table.
- Add `fn row_state_for(label: &str) -> TodoRowState`: map the status token to a
  state; for `open`, split on `parse_blocked_suffix` → Blocked/Ready;
  `not_done` → Canceled; `backlog`/`draft`/unknown → Other.
- (Optional, flagged not required) `TodoFilter` could gain chips for the new
  statuses; not needed for coloring — leave filters as-is unless wanted.

Tests (`cargo test -p panopt-zellij-logic`): `parse_blocked_suffix` true/false +
empty-title tolerance; `row_state_for` one case per state incl. open→Ready vs
open+blocked→Blocked and the two new statuses; back-compat — a pre-#236 label (no
`blocked` token) classifies open→Ready and the other suffix parsers still return
the same values when `, blocked` is appended.

### Commit 3 — plugin: thread state into rows and paint color
`crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs`
- `Item` (331-337): add `state: Option<TodoRowState>` (None for non-todo modes).
- `rebuild_items` Todos branch (~1358-1364): set
  `state: Some(panopt_zellij_logic::row_state_for(label))`; all other branches
  `state: None`.
- `Style`/`paint` (3134-3159): add an `fg: Option<u8>` param; after the existing
  `7`(focus)/`2`(dim) codes, push `38;5;{c}` when `Some` (switch `codes` to owned
  `String`s). Update all 4 call sites (664, 670, 681, 692); the row-loop passes
  `item.state.and_then(TodoRowState::fg_code)`, the rest pass `None`.

Tests (`cargo test -p panopt-zellij`, host): `paint` with `fg:Some(34)` emits
`\u{1b}[38;5;34m…`; with focus emits `7;38;5;34`; with `None` byte-identical to
today (guards existing paint tests).

### Commit 4 — new statuses across the surface
`crates/panopt-core/src/model.rs` — add `Waiting`, `NeedsReview` to `TodoStatus`
with `as_str` (`"waiting"`, `"needs_review"`) + `parse` arms.
`crates/panopt-core/src/projection.rs` — index `mark` for them stays `' '` (only
`completed`→`x`, `not_done`→`-`); per-todo file needs no change (prints `as_str`).
`crates/panoptd/src/handler.rs` — `parse_status` (617-621): add the two tokens to
the caller-facing valid-values error string.
`crates/panopt-tool-surface/src/params.rs` (TodoCreate/TodoUpdate `status` docs)
and `src/lib.rs` (TOOL_SURFACE descriptions): extend the listed values.
`DESIGN.md` / any `CLAUDE.md` status list: note the new states.

> Commit 4 is logically independent of 1–3 but small; keep it last so the color
> work lands first. If desired it can be split, but the new statuses only become
> visible (amber/purple) once Commit 2's mapping exists.

## Verification (end-to-end)

1. `cargo test` workspace-wide, then the **verify-all** skill (workspace +
   `wasm32-wasip1` plugin build + clippy `-D warnings`).
2. Manual, in a project with todos where #A blocks #B (both `open`):
   `just refresh` (rebuild + reload plugin) from a plain shell, open the Todos
   pane. Expect: **#B red** (Blocked), **#A green** (Ready), an `in_progress`
   row blue, `completed` gray, `not_done` dark gray. Set one to `waiting`
   (amber) and one to `needs_review` (purple) via `todo_update`. Then
   `todo_complete #A` → reproject fires → **#B flips green**.
3. `cat /host/.panopt/todos.md` (read-only) to confirm `, blocked` appears only
   on blocked rows.
4. Confirm the cursor/focused row (SGR `7` reverse) stays legible with a fg color
   (see risks).

## Risks

- **Index format back-compat (low):** append-only comma-token, marker only when
  blocked; a stale reader degrades open→Ready (green), never hides/misorders.
  Writer (Commit 1) + reader (Commit 2) are separate commits but each builds; if
  preferred, land them together.
- **Focus + reverse-video (med):** SGR `7` swaps fg/bg, so a colored focused row
  shows the color as background. Verify legibility in step 4; fallback is to drop
  `fg` when `focused`.
- **Terminal color support (low):** 256-color is near-universal; `fg_code`
  returning `Option<u8>` gives a clean no-color path, and state is still conveyed
  by the `[x]`/`[-]` mark + status text, so color is additive.
- **Follow-up (out of scope):** now that the index carries `blocked`,
  `TodoFilter::Active` could finally implement true "open-unblocked" instead of
  degrading to plain open (lib.rs:108-113). Flag as a separate todo; do not
  bundle.
```

80	/// records that the todo was closed without being done (cancelled,
81	/// won't-fix, superseded). Both `Completed` and `NotDone` are terminal;
82	/// only `Completed` sets `completed_at`.
83	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
84	pub enum TodoStatus {
85	    #[default]
86	    Open,
87	    InProgress,
88	    Backlog,
89	    Draft,
90	    Completed,
91	    NotDone,
92	}
93	
94	impl TodoStatus {
95	    /// The token stored in SQLite and used on the wire and in the projection.
96	    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
97	        match self {
98	            TodoStatus::Open => "open",
99	            TodoStatus::InProgress => "in_progress",
100	            TodoStatus::Backlog => "backlog",
101	            TodoStatus::Draft => "draft",
102	            TodoStatus::Completed => "completed",
103	            TodoStatus::NotDone => "not_done",
104	        }
105	    }
106	
107	    /// Parse a stored or wire token; `None` for an unrecognized string.
108	    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<TodoStatus> {
109	        match s {
110	            "open" => Some(TodoStatus::Open),
111	            "in_progress" => Some(TodoStatus::InProgress),
112	            "backlog" => Some(TodoStatus::Backlog),
113	            "draft" => Some(TodoStatus::Draft),
114	            "completed" => Some(TodoStatus::Completed),
115	            "not_done" => Some(TodoStatus::NotDone),
116	            _ => None,
117	        }
118	    }
119	}

126	    Medium,

128	}

144	            "medium" => Some(Priority::Medium),

152	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
153	pub struct TodoComment {

155	    pub id: u64,
156	    /// Display name of the agent that posted it.
157	    pub author: String,
158	    pub body: String,

161	}
162	
163	/// A todo item identified by a numeric id, unique within its project.

172	    pub body: String,
173	    pub status: TodoStatus,
174	    pub priority: Priority,
175	    /// Free-text owner; empty when unassigned. Unlike Solo's agent foreign key
176	    /// this is a plain name: PANopt's agent registry is in-memory and ephemeral
177	    /// (DESIGN.md Section 6.3), so a persisted agent id would dangle.
178	    pub assignee: String,
179	    pub tags: Vec<String>,
180	    /// Ids of other todos in the same project that block this one.
181	    pub blockers: Vec<u64>,
182	    pub comments: Vec<TodoComment>,
183	    /// SQLite `datetime('now')` text (UTC).
184	    pub created_at: String,
185	    pub updated_at: String,
186	    /// Set while `status` is `Completed`, `None` otherwise.
187	    pub completed_at: Option<String>,
188	}

191	///
192	/// Each `None` field leaves that attribute untouched; each `Some` replaces it.
193	#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]

content.text:
Confirmed by the code. Here's the precise picture:

**Yes — all 8 statuses, including the two new ones, are already fully settable.** `todo_create` (handler.rs:869) and `todo_update` (handler.rs:966) both route the `status` argument through `parse_status`, which I extended to accept `waiting` and `needs_review`. So an agent or the CLI can do `todo_update #N status=waiting` / `status=needs_review` today, with full parity to the original six. (Plus the convenience transitions `todo_start`→in_progress and `todo_complete`→completed.)

**One nuance worth flagging** — it's not specific to the new states: `status` is declared as `Option<String>` in the tool params (params.rs:88/147/169), so the generated JSON schema is just `"type": "string"`. The valid values live only in the **prose** of the tool descriptions; validation happens at **runtime** (`parse_status` returns an `invalid status '…': expected …` error for anything else). There's no schema-level `enum`, so a client doesn't get the value list machine-readably or rejected before the call. This was already true for the original six — the new two simply inherit the same model.

So nothing is under-wired. The only "should we" decision is whether to tighten that nuance:

**Option — make `status` a schema `enum`.** I could give the four status fields a real enumerated schema (the 8 values), so the set is discoverable in `tools/list` and validated client-side, not just in the description text. It's a small, self-contained change but it does make the wire schema stricter (unknown values rejected at the schema boundary instead of by `parse_status`).

Want me to do that enum tightening (folds cleanly into this #236 branch), or leave status as the runtime-validated free string it's always been?

message.content: what are all the status values? the new ones?

content.text:
All 8 status values (the wire tokens, what you pass to `status=`):

| Status | Meaning | Cockpit color |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| `open` | actionable; default on create | **green** if all blockers done (Ready), **red** if a blocker still open (Blocked) |
| `in_progress` | actively being worked | yellow |
| `waiting` | **new** — parked on something external (a person, a review, a dep outside the todo graph) | amber |
| `needs_review` | **new** — needs human judgment, approval, or clarification | purple |
| `backlog` | not yet scheduled | default |
| `draft` | early note, not committed to doing | default |
| `completed` | done (sets the `completed` timestamp) | gray |
| `not_done` | closed without completing — cancelled / won't-do / obsolete | dark gray |

**The two new ones (added in this #236 branch): `waiting` and `needs_review`.**

Note: `open`'s green/red split (Ready vs Blocked) is *derived* from the blocker graph, not a stored status — so there are **8 stored statuses** but **9 visual states**. And `not_done` already covers the todo's original "canceled/obsolete → dark gray" idea, which is why only `waiting` and `needs_review` needed to be added.

content.text:
Both questions land. Quick answers, then I'll act:

- **Filter set:** No — I didn't update it. There are **two** `TodoFilter` enums (sidebar in zellij-logic, CLI viewer in viewer.rs), each with variants All/Open/OpenUnblocked/InProgress/Backlog/Draft/Completed/NotDone — **neither has Waiting or NeedsReview**, so you can't filter to those. I'll fix it.
- **Centralizing:** No, I didn't, and you're right to flag it — adding two statuses just made me touch **6 separate hardcoded lists** (core enum, handler error, tool-surface docs, zellij-logic allow-list+filters, viewer allow-list+filters, the form). The hard constraint: **`panopt-zellij-logic` does not (and shouldn't) depend on `panopt-core`** — it's the dependency-light wasm side that works off projection strings — so the plugin's copy can't literally import `TodoStatus`. Full centralization isn't possible; a canonical `TodoStatus::ALL` + guard-tests is.
